hero.title: Grab × Navier — Koh Samui and the Gulf island triangle

markets.why_now: Air access is structurally capped - a single carrier owns the airport under a ~50-flight/day environmental limit, and Bangkok-Samui is Southeast Asia's largest single-airline city pair with some of Thailand's highest fares - so arrivals growth must route via the sea. Every sea leg today is a diesel catamaran or car ferry that the northeast monsoon suspends Gulf-wide. The White Lotus season-3 effect has made Samui the global luxury-travel story, with the Four Seasons at its center. Foiling flies above the Gulf chop, keeps schedules through marginal seas, and turns the island chain's weather-fragile transfers into smooth, near-silent hops.
markets.multimodal_fit: Grab already operates cars and bikes on Samui - in Thailand's most criticised, least competitive island ground-transport market - so a water tier slots straight into the app: GrabCar to Bangrak, Pralarn or Nathon pier, foiling hop to Phangan, Tao, Ang Thong or the mainland, Grab again at the far pier. Same app, same wallet, door-to-door.

partner_context.their_ambition: Grab is Thailand's super-app and already operates on Samui - in the country's most criticised island ground-transport market. The island trio's transfer flows (millions of one-way crossings a year) are exactly the high-value, transfer-hungry demand Grab can own end-to-end.
partner_context.their_pressure: Samui's ground transport is expensive and uncompetitive, the single ring road congests, and every marine leg is a fixed-timetable diesel ferry that the monsoon suspends Gulf-wide - the marquee trips (Phangan, Tao, Ang Thong) are the ones tourists most want and most struggle to book cleanly.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling tier in the Grab app across the triangle: Pioneer II on every corridor today (all legs 7.5-35.3 nm), with the N35 Shuttle (12-15 pax) the natural scheduled-service platform for the Donsak and inter-island volume lanes from 2027.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the piers already in use (Nathon, Bangrak, Pralarn, Lipa Noi, Thong Sala, Mae Haad, both Donsak terminals, the Four Seasons jetty). Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal. Nothing to permit, build, or wait for - in a market where the alternative mobility expansions are a capped airport and an unapproved decade-out bridge.
why_navier_now.the_moment: An N30 is live at the Four Seasons Koh Samui just as White Lotus S3 makes the island the global luxury-travel story, airport capacity is structurally capped, and the Gulf's ferries keep getting suspended by monsoon swell. The moment to own the clean island-transfer tier is now.
